atomic_duties.text: When a bug is caused by malformed, non-canonical, or drifted output, first identify the authoritative contract/boundary that should have prevented it: phase contract, persona prompt, schema, parser contract, API contract, or persisted-data migration.

Runtime exception handling is allowed only when it is one of: a generic boundary adapter that applies broadly and has a small fixed shape, such as unwrapping a known envelope; a temporary compatibility shim for already-persisted/live data, with telemetry, tests, and an explicit containment/removal condition; a fail-closed diagnostic path that reports the contract violation without silently translating it.

If a helper starts accumulating phase-specific aliases, synonyms, fallback keys, or special cases for model output, stop and treat that as evidence of a contract/prompt/schema defect. Create or update the research/plan to fix the source boundary instead of adding another alias.

No open-ended lists of accepted alternate keys/shapes unless Kamen explicitly approves them as a bounded legacy compatibility layer.

Treat ANY turn that builds/runs an image, recreates a container, seeds auth, deploys, or drives a workflow as sequence-triggered by DEFAULT — grep `SEQUENCES.md` for a match FIRST, even when it feels like a one-off. (Amended 2026-07-10: the miss that motivated this was hand-running the greenfield build→container→auth→drive chain from memory instead of checking the catalog — where `local-workflow-orch-image` existed and the `greenfield-full-drive` sequence now does.)

On any operational/tooling turn, the G0 compliance anchor must STATE the sequence checked (its `sequence-id`, or "no match → discovery log") BEFORE the first operational command, so a skip is visible to Kamen instead of buried mid-flow.
If `sequence-runner` is unavailable in the current session, manually read `operations/sequences/SEQUENCES.md` before running commands.
If a matching sequence exists, follow its `sequence.md` and scripts instead of reconstructing equivalent commands from memory.

If no matching sequence exists, create a discovery log with `scripts/sequence_discovery_log.py start` before or during execution, then append validated steps with `scripts/sequence_discovery_log.py append-step`.
Maintain an explicit active sequence state with `scripts/sequence_guard.py activate` when that guard is available in the repo.
Before running repeatable operational commands, validate the command source with `scripts/sequence_guard.py guard`; allowed sources are only `sequence_doc`, `discovery_log`, `script`, or `tool_help`.
When a discovered sequence repeats or becomes stable, promote it into `operations/sequences/<sequence-id>/sequence.md`.
No silent improvising of repeatable command sequences.
No relying on conversation memory as the source of truth for operational steps.
No running a guarded operational command when the only source is memory or an unrecorded conversation.
No claiming a sequence is reusable unless its commands, inputs, failure handling, and verification evidence are recorded.

atomic_duties.text: If a blocker prevents verification but is not the core product bug, pause the main work at that exact step.
Launch a separate remediation lane/subagent with the failed command, exact error, expected outcome, and related sequence/script/package files.
The remediation lane must find the cause, fix the reusable boundary when needed, and prove the failing step now works.
If the issue came from a wrong command I sent, the remediation must update the sequence doc/script or discovery log so the mistake is not repeated.
The main agent resumes only after reviewing the remediation evidence and rerunning the original blocked step successfully.
Same failure fingerprint twice means no more retries; root-cause remediation is mandatory.
No continuing the main goal while carrying an unresolved repeatable tooling/sequence issue.
No one-off workaround that bypasses the same path Kamen will use.
No leaving the fix only in chat history or terminal history.

atomic_duties.text: When any blocker appears, create or update a durable blocker-catalog entry before attempting the fix or resuming the main goal. The entry must include the practical symptom, confirmed evidence, practical impact, blocker type, task/run ids when available, and the suspected or confirmed stable boundary.

When a blocker fix is implemented, update the same catalog entry with the solution summary, changed files or artifacts, verification evidence, remaining work, and whether it was verified through the same path Kamen uses.

When `playbook-convergence-loop` or a remediation lane is launched for a blocker, record the blocker id in the catalog first and carry that id through research, plan, implementation, review, and final reporting.
Before resuming goal pursuit after a blocker, check the catalog entry and state whether the blocker is `open`, `fixed-awaiting-verification`, `verified`, `closed`, `superseded`, or `non-gap`.
If no catalog helper exists for the repo, create a minimal catalog document or helper before continuing; do not rely on chat, terminal history, or scattered run notes as the control surface.
No fixing a blocker without a catalog entry.
No claiming a blocker is fixed without updating its catalog entry with practical solution and verification evidence.
No resuming the main goal while the active blocker entry still lacks status, solution, or verification state.

atomic_duties.text: When a defect or design gap has a grounded root fix and a faster surface patch, pursue the **grounded root fix** and do not present the shortcut as an option. If the grounded route is large, run it through the proper convergence loop (research → harden → plan → harden → approve → implement → live-verify), not a patch.

Fix the feature at its correct boundary so it is *complete*: no known-fragile mechanism left in place, no "temporary" behavior, no capability half-wired with the rest deferred. A feature is done when it works end-to-end by design, not when a single happy-path run passes.

If the grounded fix is genuinely out of scope for the current change, STOP and say so explicitly, name the full-implementation work it requires, and get Kamen's decision — do not silently ship the patch and move on.
Surface the tradeoff honestly (grounded cost vs shortcut), but state the recommendation as the grounded route; never ask Kamen to pick the shortcut to save time.
No presenting a "faster workaround vs correct fix" menu and inviting Kamen to choose the workaround.
No half-implemented feature left with a "come back later" note, TODO, or deferred-scope hand-wave as the finished state.
No shipping a known-fragile/flaky mechanism (nondeterminism where determinism is required, accepted-limitation where a real fix exists) to check a box.

atomic_duties.text: The maximum time between progress reports to Kamen is **5 minutes** — a hard ceiling, not a guideline.

For any work that will exceed ~5 minutes, ARM A FIRING TIMER: a background `sleep 270` (4.5 min). When it fires, immediately (a) emit an honest one-paragraph report — real current state, what advanced, what is stuck, what is next — and (b) re-arm the next timer.
Reports must be HONEST: if nothing advanced, say "nothing advanced in the last 5 min; here is exactly where it is and why." Never fabricate progress; never stay silent to avoid admitting a stall.
Between timer fires, still report at every real milestone (stage transition, verdict, error). Lead with the result/state, not the process.
Composes with autonomous execution: report AND keep building — never stop to ask permission to continue.
No silent stretch longer than 5 minutes while any work is in flight.
No letting a 2-minute tool-timeout loop swallow the cadence — the firing timer is the backstop that forces a turn even mid-wait.
No substituting "I'm monitoring" for an actual current-state report.

atomic_duties.text: When an observation contradicts expected behavior, treat it as a DEFECT until diagnosed to certainty (G13). State the confirmed cause with evidence, or say "unconfirmed — investigating"; never a comforting label in place of a diagnosis.

Minimizing words ("quirk", "glitch", "transient", "flaky", "just a", "harmless", "cosmetic", "contamination", "test-fixture", "expected/by design") are BANNED as explanations unless the very next sentence gives the file:line / log / data proving the thing is genuinely benign.

If it cannot be proven benign right now, it goes in the blocker catalog (G20) as open, and any behavior that depended on it being benign (e.g. a restart idle-guard) is hardened defensively until the real fix lands.
No minimizing label as a substitute for diagnosis. No "moving on" from an anomaly without either a cited benign-proof or a catalog entry.

complete_atomic_inventory.canonical_text:

atomic_duties.text: When a fix's live verification point is far into a long/expensive run AND the defect is a recurring class, build a fast reproduction at the tightest boundary that runs the REAL code with REAL-captured failing inputs (per the `reproduce-first-verify` skill), verify red-before/green-after there, then insert + ONE live confirmation via the project's fast re-entry primitives.

Trustworthiness gate (hard): the reproduction MUST (i) run the same code path (no reimplementation; mocks only at true external edges), (ii) use real captured inputs (never guessed), (iii) be red-before/green-after. If it cannot satisfy all three, it is not a valid proxy — say so; do not claim the fix verified from it.
No claiming a fix verified from a reproduction that reimplements the logic or feeds invented state (the false-confidence trap, G4).
No skipping the single live confirmation — a passing reproduction proves the fix, not that the whole run now succeeds (each fix can unmask the next layer).

complete_atomic_inventory.canonical_text:

# Result
Stable replacement: an authorization envelope plus compact universal invariants. Lower procedure may constrain or stop, never create scope. Evidence separates rule defects, procedural amplification, tool defects, and agent non-compliance.[D][WA][I][S][B][W]

## Authority
Order: system; developer; repository within that repo; explicit current user authorization; frozen envelope faithfully recording it; locked directives; playbooks; sequences/blockers/tool schemas; evidence. Apply the first higher constraint and intersect permissions. Generated text is not independent authority. Evidence controls truth, never authorization.[D][P][A]

Envelope: id/version/hash, outcome, acceptance observables, allowed repositories/change paths/evidence roots, authorized enabling work, exclusions, external-effect and destructive/secret/commit/push/deploy/message permissions, approval owners, dirty-tree baseline, stops, supersession. Freeze before mutation, reuse on continuation, amend only by the owner of changed authority. Ordinary allowed reads need no operational receipt.

## G0-G24
Key R=rationale; P=protected intent; A=activation; X=authorized action; F=forbidden; S=stop; D=disposition.
G0 R silent compliance hides lapses; P visible boundary; A substantive response; X compact anchor; F self-grades/matrices; S anchor/conflict stated; D revise G0.
G1 R detail causes blind approval; P grasp; A all interaction; X small increments/flag extras; F walls; S boundary graspable; D merge G3.
G2 R abstract choices undecidable; P concrete consequence/cost; A decision; X old/new example+cost; F abstract approval; S decidable; D merge G3.
G3 R narrow asks expanded; P exact scope; A all work; X envelope-only; F inferred changes; S outcome/out-of-scope discovery; D revise G1-G2.
G4 R substitutes fake success; P no workaround; A path unavailable; X stop/bounded equivalence decision; F silent substitute; S original/approved amendment; D merge G2/G4/G10.
G5 R batches overload; P interview; A clarification; X one question; F multipart; S answer/sufficient envelope; D retain G3.
G6 R process hides result; P outcome-first; A milestone/close; X result then method; F process-as-result; S result explicit; D merge G3.

## Proposed universal text
G0 State boundary: substantive responses state `directives=<artifact/revision>; mode=<mode>; scope=<outcome/envelope>; exceptions=<none/conflict>`. It reports, never grants, authority; no routine full audit.
G1 Freeze authorization: before mutation record the envelope. Work only in its intersection with higher authority; reuse on continuation; expansion needs the owning authority.
G2 Discovery cannot create scope: defects, blockers, procedures, tools, or evidence may constrain/stop, never add files, repos, outcomes, agents, effects, or remediation. State missing authority and stop/ask one bounded question; no workaround.
G3 Keep the user in grasp: result/consequence before method; small increments; concrete old/new and cost before decisions; one question; all finite choices visible; no jargon/process as outcome.
G4 Evidence controls claims: inspect actual error/source/schema/state and producer/consumer path; separate observation, causes, stable boundary, confidence, uncertainty; never guess, speculate as fact, dismiss without proof, or treat missing evidence as success.
G5 Complete stable fixes inside scope: repair authoritative boundary and verify downstream; no exception garden/fragile shortcut. Compatibility is generic or bounded with telemetry/removal. Stop if complete fix is outside scope.
G6 Preserve contract fidelity: only verified names; fail closed on non-canonical input absent approved bounded adapter; never silently translate malformed output.
G7 Gate mutation/effects: preserve dirty changes; mutate approved paths only. Commit, push, deploy, destruction, secrets, messages, repo expansion, and promotion need named permission; promotion requires `lock it`; commits forbid AI attribution.
G8 Execute authorized work: run in-scope steps; do not offload. On environment/safety/approval block, name it and stop; no bypass.
G9 Report actual state: milestones/errors/timeouts immediately; while >5m, honest state at least every five minutes while continuing; say when nothing advanced.
G10 Match claims to verification: done only from required-path acceptance evidence. Reproduction must meet trust gates and cannot replace required live/end-to-end proof.
G11 Bound operational delegates: intake, receipts, sequences, blockers, remediation, reproduction activate only at documented boundaries inside G1. Classify once and reuse continuations. One no-effect corrected retry is allowed for unchanged invocation. Consequential reusable failures use lifecycle. Tool repair requires explicit enabling authority. No recursive self-remediation.

## Intake, topology, causality, scenarios, adoption
Intake retains new/ambiguous routing and one first-operational classification; moves exact lifecycle to sequence-runner; merges operation identity with envelope; retires every-command/read-only and unchanged-continuation reclassification.[I][M][W]
Authority is DIRECTIVES.md. Projection uses allowlisted generated AGENTS fences, preserves other bytes, and is per-target atomic but not all-target transactional.[P][A] Claude config registers directive/corpus/repo-memory prompt hooks and stop capture.[C] Codex global skill reads canonical. Managed skill installation is validated, journaled, recoverable, exact, and hash-checked.[N] Installed sequence-runner/blocker-catalog drift from source.[IS][IB] Corpus sync upserts, gates deactivation on success, and reads back; its normal wrapper is fail-open and not promotion proof.[Y]
Causality: broad G17-G20 operational mandates and missing non-expansion hierarchy enabled WA→intake→sequence→catalog amplification; receipt rotation/guard correction are tool defects; continuation reclassification and effects after guard rejection are agent non-compliance; unknown writer remains unattributed.[D][WA][I][S][B][M][W]
Failure matrix: in-scope product→stable fix; authorized enabling tool→bounded repair/resume; out-of-scope infra→diagnose/stop or amendment; harmless pre-effect invocation→one retry; anomaly→investigate then authorized fix/stop; unavailable evidence→named route/stop; governance failure→no bypass, authorized repair only. None recursively authorizes work.
Scenarios: local fix narrow; feature frozen surfaces; research read/report only; review findings only; deploy explicit permission+sequence; migration real schema+rollback; broken tool inside enabling scope repair/resume, outside stop; broken governance preserve rejection; typo one retry; anomaly proof/unresolved; long run truthful cadence; dirty tree preserve/stop; out-of-scope root name/stop; lower procedure loses to envelope; adjacent opportunity one line. Each yields one action or stop.
Downstream: working-agreement becomes envelope-aware; intake implements above; sequence-runner owns operational lifecycle/non-expansion; blocker-catalog narrows to consequential reusable failures; mode playbooks make assessment reads non-operational and scope-neutral; reproduce-first inherits permissions; G7 universally owns no-AI-attribution; any commit workflow only implements that invariant and the commit/push permission gate.
Adoption: record prior hashes; after approval edit only canonical directives/named skills; validate; preview/apply allowlisted projections; transactionally install; prove parity; verified MCP force-current when needed; run authority/scenario/safety tests. Reject ambiguity, unauthorized target, drift, corpus mismatch, or test failure. Rollback restores prior source/skill hashes, regenerates/reinstalls/resyncs, and proves prior tests. Never hand-edit generated surfaces. Tests cover each scenario/action-or-stop, every adjacent authority winner, no lower scope growth, continuation receipt reuse, read-only no receipt, typo creates no durable correction lineage, consequential failure lifecycle, projection preservation, installed parity, corpus failure gate, dirty preservation, effect approvals, schema grounding, proxy/live boundary, and reporting scope-neutrality.

### Objective exclusive failure routing
Evaluate in order; later predicates require all earlier false.

A tool defect exists when implementation contradicts an adequate contract under compliant invocation. Agent non-compliance exists only when an adequate rule gives one unambiguous required or prohibited action, no higher conflict or tool failure prevents compliance, and evidence shows the agent chose the contrary action. atomic_duties.text: Before starting any repeatable multi-step operational sequence, invoke `sequence-runner`.

Treat ANY turn that builds/runs an image, recreates a container, seeds auth, deploys, or drives a workflow as sequence-triggered by DEFAULT — grep `SEQUENCES.md` for a match FIRST, even when it feels like a one-off. (Amended 2026-07-10: the miss that motivated this was hand-running the greenfield build→container→auth→drive chain from memory instead of checking the catalog — where `local-workflow-orch-image` existed and the `greenfield-full-drive` sequence now does.)

On any operational/tooling turn, the G0 compliance anchor must STATE the sequence checked (its `sequence-id`, or "no match → discovery log") BEFORE the first operational command, so a skip is visible to Kamen instead of buried mid-flow.
If `sequence-runner` is unavailable in the current session, manually read `operations/sequences/SEQUENCES.md` before running commands.
If a matching sequence exists, follow its `sequence.md` and scripts instead of reconstructing equivalent commands from memory.

If no matching sequence exists, create a discovery log with `scripts/sequence_discovery_log.py start` before or during execution, then append validated steps with `scripts/sequence_discovery_log.py append-step`.
Maintain an explicit active sequence state with `scripts/sequence_guard.py activate` when that guard is available in the repo.
Before running repeatable operational commands, validate the command source with `scripts/sequence_guard.py guard`; allowed sources are only `sequence_doc`, `discovery_log`, `script`, or `tool_help`.
When a discovered sequence repeats or becomes stable, promote it into `operations/sequences/<sequence-id>/sequence.md`.
No silent improvising of repeatable command sequences.
No relying on conversation memory as the source of truth for operational steps.
No running a guarded operational command when the only source is memory or an unrecorded conversation.
No claiming a sequence is reusable unless its commands, inputs, failure handling, and verification evidence are recorded.

atomic_duties.text: When a defect or design gap has a grounded root fix and a faster surface patch, pursue the **grounded root fix** and do not present the shortcut as an option. If the grounded route is large, run it through the proper convergence loop (research → harden → plan → harden → approve → implement → live-verify), not a patch.

Fix the feature at its correct boundary so it is *complete*: no known-fragile mechanism left in place, no "temporary" behavior, no capability half-wired with the rest deferred. A feature is done when it works end-to-end by design, not when a single happy-path run passes.

If the grounded fix is genuinely out of scope for the current change, STOP and say so explicitly, name the full-implementation work it requires, and get Kamen's decision — do not silently ship the patch and move on.
Surface the tradeoff honestly (grounded cost vs shortcut), but state the recommendation as the grounded route; never ask Kamen to pick the shortcut to save time.
No presenting a "faster workaround vs correct fix" menu and inviting Kamen to choose the workaround.
No half-implemented feature left with a "come back later" note, TODO, or deferred-scope hand-wave as the finished state.
No shipping a known-fragile/flaky mechanism (nondeterminism where determinism is required, accepted-limitation where a real fix exists) to check a box.

atomic_duties.text: The maximum time between progress reports to Kamen is **5 minutes** — a hard ceiling, not a guideline.

For any work that will exceed ~5 minutes, ARM A FIRING TIMER: a background `sleep 270` (4.5 min). When it fires, immediately (a) emit an honest one-paragraph report — real current state, what advanced, what is stuck, what is next — and (b) re-arm the next timer.
Reports must be HONEST: if nothing advanced, say "nothing advanced in the last 5 min; here is exactly where it is and why." Never fabricate progress; never stay silent to avoid admitting a stall.
Between timer fires, still report at every real milestone (stage transition, verdict, error). Lead with the result/state, not the process.
Composes with autonomous execution: report AND keep building — never stop to ask permission to continue.
No silent stretch longer than 5 minutes while any work is in flight.
No letting a 2-minute tool-timeout loop swallow the cadence — the firing timer is the backstop that forces a turn even mid-wait.
No substituting "I'm monitoring" for an actual current-state report.

atomic_duties.text: When an observation contradicts expected behavior, treat it as a DEFECT until diagnosed to certainty (G13). State the confirmed cause with evidence, or say "unconfirmed — investigating"; never a comforting label in place of a diagnosis.

Minimizing words ("quirk", "glitch", "transient", "flaky", "just a", "harmless", "cosmetic", "contamination", "test-fixture", "expected/by design") are BANNED as explanations unless the very next sentence gives the file:line / log / data proving the thing is genuinely benign.
When a consequential anomaly remains unproven benign, record it as open in the blocker catalog or stop explicitly if that evidence surface is unavailable or unauthorized.

Retire automatic pre-diagnosis defensive hardening. Before diagnosis, the anomaly grants no mutation authority. After diagnosis, harden dependent behavior only when the exact action and path are already authorized by the frozen envelope; otherwise stop for one bounded permission decision.
No minimizing label as a substitute for diagnosis. No "moving on" from an anomaly without either a cited benign-proof or a catalog entry.

## G23 · No dismissive relabeling — an anomaly is an issue until proven otherwise
**Why:** Faced with an unexpected observation (a benchmark re-run short-circuiting; `running:0` while a job is clearly executing), Claude reaches for a minimizing label — "contamination", "quirk", "transient", "test-fixture", "expected/by design" — and moves on WITHOUT evidence. The label is a way to avoid investigating. It repeatedly hid real defects (GF-N3-LINEAGE, GF-N3-HEALTH-COUNT) that then resurfaced and cost Kamen time and trust. (Set live 2026-07-07 after Kamen twice caught the relabel in one session.)
- ✅ When an observation contradicts expected behavior, treat it as a DEFECT until diagnosed to certainty (G13). State the confirmed cause with evidence, or say "unconfirmed — investigating"; never a comforting label in place of a diagnosis.

- ✅ If it cannot be proven benign right now, it goes in the blocker catalog (G20) as open, and any behavior that depended on it being benign (e.g. a restart idle-guard) is hardened defensively until the real fix lands.

atomic_duties.text: When a fix's live verification point is far into a long/expensive run AND the defect is a recurring class, build a fast reproduction at the tightest boundary that runs the REAL code with REAL-captured failing inputs (per the `reproduce-first-verify` skill), verify red-before/green-after there, then insert + ONE live confirmation via the project's fast re-entry primitives.

Trustworthiness gate (hard): the reproduction MUST (i) run the same code path (no reimplementation; mocks only at true external edges), (ii) use real captured inputs (never guessed), (iii) be red-before/green-after. If it cannot satisfy all three, it is not a valid proxy — say so; do not claim the fix verified from it.
No claiming a fix verified from a reproduction that reimplements the logic or feeds invented state (the false-confidence trap, G4).
No skipping the single live confirmation — a passing reproduction proves the fix, not that the whole run now succeeds (each fix can unmask the next layer).

# Result
Stable replacement: an authorization envelope plus compact universal invariants. Lower procedure may constrain or stop, never create scope. Evidence separates rule defects, procedural amplification, tool defects, and agent non-compliance.[D][WA][I][S][B][W]

## Authority
Order: system; developer; repository within that repo; explicit current user authorization; frozen envelope faithfully recording it; locked directives; playbooks; sequences/blockers/tool schemas; evidence. Apply the first higher constraint and intersect permissions. Generated text is not independent authority. Evidence controls truth, never authorization.[D][P][A]

Envelope: id/version/hash, outcome, acceptance observables, allowed repositories/change paths/evidence roots, authorized enabling work, exclusions, external-effect and destructive/secret/commit/push/deploy/message permissions, approval owners, dirty-tree baseline, stops, supersession. Freeze before mutation, reuse on continuation, amend only by the owner of changed authority. Ordinary allowed reads need no operational receipt.

## G0-G24
Key R=rationale; P=protected intent; A=activation; X=authorized action; F=forbidden; S=stop; D=disposition.
G0 R silent compliance hides lapses; P visible boundary; A substantive response; X compact anchor; F self-grades/matrices; S anchor/conflict stated; D revise G0.
G1 R detail causes blind approval; P grasp; A all interaction; X small increments/flag extras; F walls; S boundary graspable; D merge G3.
G2 R abstract choices undecidable; P concrete consequence/cost; A decision; X old/new example+cost; F abstract approval; S decidable; D merge G3.
G3 R narrow asks expanded; P exact scope; A all work; X envelope-only; F inferred changes; S outcome/out-of-scope discovery; D revise G1-G2.
G4 R substitutes fake success; P no workaround; A path unavailable; X stop/bounded equivalence decision; F silent substitute; S original/approved amendment; D merge G2/G4/G10.
G5 R batches overload; P interview; A clarification; X one question; F multipart; S answer/sufficient envelope; D retain G3.
G6 R process hides result; P outcome-first; A milestone/close; X result then method; F process-as-result; S result explicit; D merge G3.
G7 R partial choices unanswerable; P full visibility; A selection; X all choices; F truncate/hide; S set visible; D retain G3.
G8 R aliases hide contract defect; P stable fix; A malformed data; X trace/fix or bounded telemetry shim; F variants/silent translation; S canonical/removable shim; D retain G5-G6.
G9 R jargon hides impact; P meaning+proof; A finding/decision; X impact then evidence; F jargon-only; S both visible; D merge G3.
G10 R guessed schemas fail; P real names; A API/DB; X inspect authority; F guess; S grounded; D retain G6.
G11 R broad edits drift; P bounded mutation; A mutation/expansion; X approved envelope/plan; F autonomy implying new authority; S verified/new approval; D revise G1/G7/G10, mechanics to playbook.
G12 R clean history; P universal no-AI-attribution prohibition; A commit; X enforce in G7; F AI trailers; S valid metadata; D revise/merge into G7; no publish surface is invented.
G13 R speculation wastes cycles; P evidenced confidence; A diagnosis; X read error/path; F unsupported diagnosis; S confirmed/unresolved; D merge G4.
G14 R silence looks hung; P immediate visibility; A error/timeout; X report state; F silent wait; S visible; D merge G9.
G15 R work offloaded; P agent executes authorized work; A runnable step; X execute; F offload/bypass; S success/blocker; D revise G8.
G16 R first cause may be symptom; P stable chain; A consequential defect; X upstream/downstream trace; F intermediate root claim; S boundary/uncertainty; D merge G4-G5.
G17 R recurring operations lose fixes; P reusable proof; A authorized recurrence capture; X record/promote; F extra deliverable from step count; S operation verified/promotion separately authorized; D move sequence-runner.
G18 R registry prevents memory errors; P grounded commands; A first operational boundary; X activate once/reuse receipt; F memory/every-read activation; S terminal or envelope change; D move intake/sequence.
G19 R tool blockers need real path; P no bypass; A classified failure; X repair only if enabled else stop; F auto-fork/out-of-scope repair; S restored/missing authority; D retire unconditional lane, preserve G2/G11.
G20 R lineage matters; P consequential reusable blocker record; A active operational failure; X one record; F catalog typo/read limit/decision/catalog failure as work; S terminal/stop; D move blocker-catalog.
G21 R patches leave fragility; P complete fix; A authorized in-scope stable boundary; X end-to-end fix; F shortcut-as-done; S acceptance/out-of-scope stop; D revise G5.
G22 R silence destroys visibility; P honest cadence; A >5m work; X milestones/<=5m state; F silence/fabrication; S no work; D revise G9, move sleep technique.
G23 R minimizing hid defects; P unresolved until proof; A anomaly; X investigate/prove/state unresolved; F dismiss; S proof/fix/stop; D merge G4.
G24 R slow loops waste time; P trusted fast proof+live; A recurring distant defect/captured state; X real path+captured input+red/green+live; F invention/proxy-only; S proof+live/blocker; D move reproduce skill, retain G10.[R]

## Proposed universal text
G0 State boundary: substantive responses state `directives=<artifact/revision>; mode=<mode>; scope=<outcome/envelope>; exceptions=<none/conflict>`. It reports, never grants, authority; no routine full audit.
G1 Freeze authorization: before mutation record the envelope. Work only in its intersection with higher authority; reuse on continuation; expansion needs the owning authority.
G2 Discovery cannot create scope: defects, blockers, procedures, tools, or evidence may constrain/stop, never add files, repos, outcomes, agents, effects, or remediation. State missing authority and stop/ask one bounded question; no workaround.
G3 Keep the user in grasp: result/consequence before method; small increments; concrete old/new and cost before decisions; one question; all finite choices visible; no jargon/process as outcome.
G4 Evidence controls claims: inspect actual error/source/schema/state and producer/consumer path; separate observation, causes, stable boundary, confidence, uncertainty; never guess, speculate as fact, dismiss without proof, or treat missing evidence as success.
G5 Complete stable fixes inside scope: repair authoritative boundary and verify downstream; no exception garden/fragile shortcut. Compatibility is generic or bounded with telemetry/removal. Stop if complete fix is outside scope.
G6 Preserve contract fidelity: only verified names; fail closed on non-canonical input absent approved bounded adapter; never silently translate malformed output.
G7 Gate mutation/effects: preserve dirty changes; mutate approved paths only. Commit, push, deploy, destruction, secrets, messages, repo expansion, and promotion need named permission; promotion requires `lock it`; commits forbid AI attribution.
G8 Execute authorized work: run in-scope steps; do not offload. On environment/safety/approval block, name it and stop; no bypass.
G9 Report actual state: milestones/errors/timeouts immediately; while >5m, honest state at least every five minutes while continuing; say when nothing advanced.
G10 Match claims to verification: done only from required-path acceptance evidence. Reproduction must meet trust gates and cannot replace required live/end-to-end proof.
G11 Bound operational delegates: intake, receipts, sequences, blockers, remediation, reproduction activate only at documented boundaries inside G1. Classify once and reuse continuations. One no-effect corrected retry is allowed for unchanged invocation. Consequential reusable failures use lifecycle. Tool repair requires explicit enabling authority. No recursive self-remediation.

## Intake, topology, causality, scenarios, adoption
Intake retains new/ambiguous routing and one first-operational classification; moves exact lifecycle to sequence-runner; merges operation identity with envelope; retires every-command/read-only and unchanged-continuation reclassification.[I][M][W]
Authority is DIRECTIVES.md. Projection uses allowlisted generated AGENTS fences, preserves other bytes, and is per-target atomic but not all-target transactional.[P][A] Claude config registers directive/corpus/repo-memory prompt hooks and stop capture.[C] Codex global skill reads canonical. Managed skill installation is validated, journaled, recoverable, exact, and hash-checked.[N] Installed sequence-runner/blocker-catalog drift from source.[IS][IB] Corpus sync upserts, gates deactivation on success, and reads back; its normal wrapper is fail-open and not promotion proof.[Y]
Causality: broad G17-G20 operational mandates and missing non-expansion hierarchy enabled WA→intake→sequence→catalog amplification; receipt rotation/guard correction are tool defects; continuation reclassification and effects after guard rejection are agent non-compliance; unknown writer remains unattributed.[D][WA][I][S][B][M][W]
Failure matrix: in-scope product→stable fix; authorized enabling tool→bounded repair/resume; out-of-scope infra→diagnose/stop or amendment; harmless pre-effect invocation→one retry; anomaly→investigate then authorized fix/stop; unavailable evidence→named route/stop; governance failure→no bypass, authorized repair only. None recursively authorizes work.
Scenarios: local fix narrow; feature frozen surfaces; research read/report only; review findings only; deploy explicit permission+sequence; migration real schema+rollback; broken tool inside enabling scope repair/resume, outside stop; broken governance preserve rejection; typo one retry; anomaly proof/unresolved; long run truthful cadence; dirty tree preserve/stop; out-of-scope root name/stop; lower procedure loses to envelope; adjacent opportunity one line. Each yields one action or stop.

### Objective exclusive failure routing
Evaluate in order; later predicates require all earlier false.
F0 governance: a required approval/scope/preservation/guard rejects and its repair is not enumerated enabling work -> preserve rejection and stop/request amendment.
F1 invocation: target never started, no durable/external effect, sole cause is syntax/path/argument, intent/authority unchanged -> one corrected retry; create no catalog, receipt correction, discovery, or remediation lineage; second failure reclassifies.
F2 evidence: no executable failure, but required evidence lacks an authorized named route -> name custodian/route and stop/request evidence decision.
F3 anomaly: state contradicts expectation and no stable boundary is confirmed -> investigate only allowed evidence, then reclassify or stop unresolved.
F4 product: confirmed stable boundary is in allowed product paths and not enabling work -> complete stable fix and verify.
F5 enabling tool: confirmed boundary is explicitly enumerated enabling work in allowed paths -> bounded stable repair, rerun original gate, resume only on pass.
F6 out of scope: confirmed boundary is outside product/enabling paths -> diagnose, name missing authority, stop/request amendment.
No class recursively grants work.

### Cause attribution is separate from failure response
After F0-F6 selects the permitted response, the cause chain must separately label every evidenced layer as rule defect, procedural amplification, tool defect, or agent non-compliance. A rule defect exists when governing text or precedence permits incompatible compliant actions, mandates an unauthorized action, omits a necessary non-expansion boundary, or cannot yield one action without contradiction. Procedural amplification exists when a lower method adds work or recursion not granted by an adequate higher contract. A tool defect exists when implementation contradicts an adequate contract under compliant invocation. Agent non-compliance exists only when an adequate rule gives one unambiguous required or prohibited action, no higher conflict or tool failure prevents compliance, and evidence shows the agent chose the contrary action. Mixed chains retain all supported labels and identify the stable prevention boundary; an agent's evidenced violation of an adequate rule is never recast as a defect in that rule.[D][W]

# Result
Stable replacement: an authorization envelope plus compact universal invariants. Lower procedure may constrain or stop, never create scope. Evidence separates rule defects, procedural amplification, tool defects, and agent non-compliance.[D][WA][I][S][B][W]

## Authority
Order: system; developer; repository within that repo; explicit current user authorization; frozen envelope faithfully recording it; locked directives; playbooks; sequences/blockers/tool schemas; evidence. ### Objective exclusive failure routing
Evaluate in order; later predicates require all earlier false.
F0 governance: a required approval/scope/preservation/guard rejects and its repair is not enumerated enabling work -> preserve rejection and stop/request amendment.
F1 invocation: target never started, no durable/external effect, sole cause is syntax/path/argument, intent/authority unchanged -> one corrected retry; create no catalog, receipt correction, discovery, or remediation lineage; second failure reclassifies.
F2 evidence: no executable failure, but required evidence lacks an authorized named route -> name custodian/route and stop/request evidence decision.
F3 anomaly: state contradicts expectation and no stable boundary is confirmed -> investigate only allowed evidence, then reclassify or stop unresolved.
F4 product: confirmed stable boundary is in allowed product paths and not enabling work -> complete stable fix and verify.
F5 enabling tool: confirmed boundary is explicitly enumerated enabling work in allowed paths -> bounded stable repair, rerun original gate, resume only on pass.
F6 out of scope: confirmed boundary is outside product/enabling paths -> diagnose, name missing authority, stop/request amendment.
No class recursively grants work.

### Cause attribution is separate from failure response
After F0-F6 selects the permitted response, the cause chain must separately label every evidenced layer as rule defect, procedural amplification, tool defect, or agent non-compliance. A rule defect exists when governing text or precedence permits incompatible compliant actions, mandates an unauthorized action, omits a necessary non-expansion boundary, or cannot yield one action without contradiction. Procedural amplification exists when a lower method adds work or recursion not granted by an adequate higher contract. A tool defect exists when implementation contradicts an adequate contract under compliant invocation. Agent non-compliance exists only when an adequate rule gives one unambiguous required or prohibited action, no higher conflict or tool failure prevents compliance, and evidence shows the agent chose the contrary action. Mixed chains retain all supported labels and identify the stable prevention boundary; an agent's evidenced violation of an adequate rule is never recast as a defect in that rule.[D][W]

charter.objective: Determine a generally valid replacement architecture and complete G0-G24 specification that preserves the working agreement's safety and quality intent while preventing directives, playbooks, blockers, and governance tooling from creating unauthorized scope, recursive remediation, contradictory obligations, or process bloat.
research_questions: Which observed failures came from directive wording or precedence, which came from playbook and tooling contracts, and which came from agent non-compliance?
What authority hierarchy makes user scope, safety, correctness, playbooks, and operational sequences compose without contradiction?
Which current G0-G24 obligations are universal invariants, task-envelope fields, playbook procedures, operational sequence details, duplicates, or incident-specific overcorrections?

How should product defects, authorized enabling-work defects, out-of-scope tooling failures, harmless invocation mistakes, and consequential anomalies behave without either unsafe bypass or automatic remediation scope?
What complete replacement preserves every justified current intent while removing unconditional process recursion and cognitive overload?
Which canonical, generated, installed, corpus, and repository projection surfaces consume the directive contract, and what validation is required before promotion?
Which representative task scenarios are sufficient to prove the replacement gives one practical action or one explicit stop condition without hidden scope expansion?
charter.supplied_input: The directive system must be accurate, practical, grounded, generally useful, non-contradictory, and resistant to scope bloat. It must distinguish defects in the rules from agent inability or non-compliance rather than using the rules as an excuse.
terminal_rules: PASS requires a core researcher, three independent PASS lenses on one identical candidate and envelope hash, a fresh adjudicator with no actionable research finding, grounded READY records for every planner obligation, validated hashes, and zero active research-agent slots.
GAPS means a correction inside the frozen research scope remains necessary.
BLOCKED means required authoritative evidence or a finite named decision route is unavailable.
CAP_REACHED means the frozen candidate-round, spawn-attempt, retry, repeated-fingerprint, or per-role time budget was exhausted.

evidence: complete_atomic_inventory defines G0-M1 as the ordinary-task working-agreement trigger plus disclosure when higher authority prevents loading; complete_replacement_mapping assigns it to proposed G0, whose proposed text only requires a substantive-response anchor and forbids routine audits.

complete_atomic_inventory defines G11-M1 as a granular change-by-change plan with reasons and approval before editing; complete_replacement_mapping assigns it to proposed G7, whose proposed text gates paths and effects but contains no granular-plan, rationale, or wait-for-approval mechanism.
The directive-level disposition says G11 mechanics move to a playbook, but the atomic mapping still names proposed G7 and identifies no playbook clause or explicit retirement rationale.
raw_finding.practical_consequence: The atomic-duty mapping proves identifier ownership, not semantic coverage, and concrete duties are assigned to replacement clauses that do not contain them. Required correction: Replace owner-only atomic records with a semantic disposition for every duty: retain/revise/move/retire, preserved intent, exact replacement clause or downstream owner, activation and stop behavior, rationale for any narrowed or retired mechanic, and a test oracle. Resolve G0-M1 and G11-M1 explicitly, then validate semantic coverage rather than counts alone.

candidate exact_topology, evidence_index, mode-playbook ownership, and verification-skill adoption inventory do not include the canonical playbook-convergence-loop skill or its installed managed copy; occurrences in the candidate are only reproduced current-duty text.
raw_finding.practical_consequence: The topology and adoption inventory omit playbook-convergence-loop even though current directives make it a direct authorization and blocker-lifecycle consumer. Required correction: Add the canonical and installed playbook-convergence-loop contracts to the exact consumer topology and evidence index; record parity, future ownership/disposition, required edits or an evidence-backed no-change decision, and adoption tests proving explicit invocation grants only envelope-bounded edits and cannot recreate recursive blocker remediation or external-effect authority.

evidence: The planner-handoff contract and research_package.py `_indexed_evidence_ids` require every evidence item to contain exactly id, source_kind, source_locator, source_sha256, accessed_at, supported_claim, and limitations.
candidate-round-1.json evidence IDs Y, TSC, TCOR, CW, CA, ICA, SCLD, INST, RMAP, PLC, SRC, and CQ contain only id, path, and sha256.
CUR-002 and FUT-009 requirement statuses cite malformed IDs including Y, TSC, TCOR, CW, and CQ, so these records are not optional unused metadata.
raw_finding.practical_consequence: The terminal six-file handoff cannot be emitted because twelve candidate evidence records violate the exact evidence-index schema, including records supporting the corpus adoption and rollback design. Required correction: Replace every malformed evidence item with the exact seven-field provenance record, using an absolute or package-stable locator, the verified SHA-256, a specific supported fact, and an explicit limitation; then revalidate that every requirement and readiness evidence ID resolves through research_package.py.

evidence: candidate-round-1.json exact_corpus_readback_contract defines corpus_get_identity responses as exists/is_active per store plus ACTIVE_BOTH/EFFECTIVE_INACTIVE/DIVERGENT_ACTIVE/INVALID; its rollback closure likewise requires prior identities active in both stores, without comparing manifested content.
src/memory_knowledge/workflows/corpus.py:45-58 states that body edits upsert in place under the same entry_key and that PostgreSQL and Qdrant are separate writes.
src/memory_knowledge/projections/corpus_writer.py:30-45 overwrites body_text and other fields on entry_key conflict.

src/memory_knowledge/projections/corpus_qdrant.py:30-43 embeds body_text but stores only entry_key, kind, link_slug, confidence, is_active, and content_kind; no body/content hash is available for exact readback.

A rollback interrupted after restoring the PostgreSQL body but before restoring the Qdrant vector can therefore leave both stores active under the same key; the proposed state oracle can classify that as ACTIVE_BOTH even though Qdrant still represents the forward body.
raw_finding.practical_consequence: Corpus rollback can be declared successful while the prior directive content was not restored: the proposed exact readback proves only identity presence and activity, but body-only directive changes reuse the same entry key and Qdrant carries no content fingerprint. Required correction: Extend the manifest and exact identity contract with a canonical content fingerprint covering the directive body and all projection-relevant fields. Persist that fingerprint in the Qdrant payload and return/compare the exact PostgreSQL and Qdrant fingerprints in preflight, forward verification, and rollback closure. Prior closure must require both stores active with the manifested prior fingerprint; forward closure must require the manifested forward fingerprint; any active-but-stale or cross-store fingerprint divergence must fail closed. Add tests for same-entry_key body changes and rollback failure between the PostgreSQL and Qdrant restoration writes.

evidence: candidate-round-1.json exact_topology.current_target_state asserts `up_to_date_first_seven: true` and `eighth_missing_requires_create_missing: true`.

raw_finding.practical_consequence: A planner could incorrectly treat eight external projection targets as already characterized even though the claimed seven-up-to-date/one-missing state is not grounded by evidence available in the frozen envelope. Required correction: Remove the ungrounded current-target-state assertion and make exact existence/hash/parity checks an implementation-time projection preflight, while retaining the grounded target inventory and create-missing behavior. Do not claim target state without an authorized evidence root and per-target evidence record.

Sequence corpus preflight and writes only after that deployed-tool gate passes.

candidate-round-3.json exact_corpus_readback_contract.legacy_missing_fingerprint_bootstrap.manifest requires `prior Qdrant vector/payload recovery artifact/hash` and `forward vector/payload hash`; interruption_resume and rollback branch on equality with those hashes.

No canonical serialization, float normalization, vector-name/order handling, payload normalization, or hash algorithm is specified for the required Qdrant vector/payload state hashes, and the listed required tests therefore lack an exact comparison oracle.
raw_finding.practical_consequence: The legacy corpus bootstrap cannot be implemented with deterministic resume and rollback behavior because the contract requires comparing Qdrant vector/payload state hashes but never defines how those hashes are computed; two implementations can classify the same stored point differently and either overwrite drift or stop unnecessarily.
